summary: Tidebreak's screens over the ring (RoundScreen after each round, MatchScreen at the match's end), the loading screen's tips on the way into the ring, Quick match's line, and the practice dummy (RingMode's practice: a dummy of a chosen element that stands, blocks or throws; no timer, no rounds; R puts both back at their ends). Plain words only, none from any show (tests/ring/test_player_words.gd reads every string here). The owner, 2026-10-05: 'games not bad', 'it is fun'; catching a stone just before it hits and firing it back is the fun core, so practice is for trying moves and catching.

round._doc: RoundScreen (scripts/ui/round_screen.gd): who took the round and why, the score, a short tally of the round (no replay). %s is the other side's name (Stone, Tide, Ember, Gale); the round number %d.
round.why_win_ringout: Into the water: you knocked the %s off the end
round.why_loss_ringout: Into the water: knocked off your end
round.why_win_winded: Winded: the %s was spent in the last zone
round.why_loss_winded: Winded: you were spent in your last zone
round.why_win_territory: Ground held: at the bell you stood nearer the middle
round.why_loss_territory: Ground held: at the bell the %s stood nearer the middle
round.why_win_health: Level ground at the bell, and you stood stronger
round.why_loss_health: Level ground at the bell, and the %s stood stronger
round.why_draw_time: Level ground and level strength at the bell
round.why_win_knockout: Knockout: every one of them in the water
round.why_loss_knockout: Knockout: your whole side in the water

match._doc: MatchScreen (scripts/ui/match_screen.gd) at the match's end: the result, the score, a line for each round, the match's tally; Rematch, your element and the opponent for the rematch, the main menu.
match.totals: The match  ·  your casts %d  ·  catches %d  ·  knock-backs %d
match.rematch_line: the same setup, the score nil

practice._doc: RingMode's practice (MatchSetup.kind practice; the user arg practice=stand|block|throw). The dummy is a bot of the chosen element held at its end: 'stand' never casts; 'block' answers what comes at it with its element's guards (catch, deflect, redirect, parry, shield: no dice, every time its lock fits) and raises its cover when you begin a lock (cover, at most every block_every_s); 'throw' casts its throw at you every throw_every_s (earth a stone spike: catch it and send it back). No timer, no rounds, the soft walls off (walk anywhere); a fall into the water puts both back at their ends after reset_after_out_s; R (ring_reset) puts them back at once, B (ring_dummy) steps the dummy's way. Spent at 0 health: whole again at once.

ways.block: blocks: its guards and its cover
ways.throw: throws at you every few seconds

words.hint: Practice  ·  a %s dummy that %s  ·  R: reset positions  ·  B: stand, block or throw  ·  Esc: menu
words.out: Into the water: back to your ends

tips: Knock the other side back through its three zones and off the open end into the water to take the round.
Pushed back over a line, you are held to that zone for the rest of the round.
You may step into their half only once all of them are pushed back.
At the bell, the side holding more ground takes the round; on level ground, the stronger side.
Spent at nothing, you are not out: you are pushed back a zone and get your breath back.
A stone flying at you can be caught just before it hits and sent straight back.
A jet of water wears an earth wall down fast.
Fire melts an ice wall, and leaves water behind to draw on.
A water bubble stops fire and air, but not stone.
An air shield sends light bolts back; a stone goes through it.
Only fire can turn lightning back on its caster.
The grates on the zone lines refill your water.
A hit taken breaks your lock: cast from behind cover.
Two walls each at most: a third crumbles your oldest.
Q puts your readied move on the left button for quick casts.
Practice from the main menu: a dummy that stands, blocks or throws, no timer.
